images.author: Jerrye & Roy Klotz, MD
images.caption: AKA PFOUTZ HOUSE, PIONEER FARM, AND STARKS WILDERNESS CENTER PIONEER FARM;  BUILT IN 1820 BY REUBEN PFOUTZ WHO BOUGHT IT FROM HIS BROTHER GEORGE.  IT IS OWNED BY THE WILDERNESS CENTER BUT IS LIVED IN

facade.notes: a two-storey house of large squared sandstone blocks, side-gabled with interior end chimneys and louvred attic vents in the gable; a one-storey kitchen wing with a red standing-seam roof runs off one side with a long shed-roofed work porch (wash tubs, buckets); the farmyard lawn runs right up to the walls

why.note: the two-storey, one-room-deep farm house of the Pennsylvania-Ohio stream (Kniffen)
local sandstone quarried on or near the farm
the kitchen and work porch in a lower wing: summer kitchen heat and farm work kept out of the main block
